newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Christian Dems happy with budget talks - CTK.
newsitem.headline: Czech Christian Dems happy with budget talks - CTK.

text.p: The Czech Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), a key party in the centre-right government, are happy with the outcome of emergency budget talks ahead of a government confidence vote later on Tuesday, Czech news agency CTK reported.
The outcome of the talks was widely seen as a test of the government's ability to unite ahead of the confidence vote.
After more then seven hours of negotiations, lasting into the early hours of Tuesday, the government agreed to cut 20 billion crowns from the 1997 state budget.

Josef Lux, the leader of KDU-CSL, a centrist party whose support is vital to the survival of monetarist Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's coalition government, was reported by CTK as being content with the deal in spite of a decision not to postpone deregulation of energy prices and rents.

Lux had wanted a postponement of the deregulations, planned for July 1, to soften the impact of budget cuts which he had insisted upon to balance the budget. According to CTK, he accepted defeat on the issue with equanimity.
"If parliament does not decide otherwise, then the deregulations will go ahead," Lux was quoted by CTK as saying.
Parliament is due to begin debating a confidence motion in the government later on Tuesday.

The attitude of KDU-CSL, which has openly criticised Klaus's style of government and which has not ruled out joining up with the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), could determine the fate of the government in Tuesday's vote.
